title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in - Merchant Holdings
summary: Quarterly renewal check-in focused on Dedicated capacity upgrade, adding EU region, and contract extension options. Customer requests updated pricing, security docs, and a benchmark run for 2x capacity with VPC/KMS configuration.
next_steps: Samira to send Dedicated 2x pricing and contract extension options by 2027-01-27
Evan to schedule benchmark run with customer's sample workload w/c 2027-01-25

transcript:
Header: 2027-01-20 15:00 PST | Duration: 52 mins
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Evan Martinez (Redwood SE), Rohit Desai (Redwood CSM), Lydia Chen (MH Head MLOps), Marcus Lee (MH CTO), Priya Singh (MH Platform), Tom Alvarez (MH Procurement)

00:00 Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick agenda — renewal check, capacity needs, adding EU region, and any security or procurement blockers.
00:18 Lydia: Thanks, Samira. Quick context — we're at 75% of our current Dedicated pool during US peak, and with new merchants onboarding we expect 1.8-2x load by Q2. So main ask is options for capacity and latency targets.
00:35 Marcus: Also, we're expanding into EU and need region support + data residency controls.
00:42 Evan: Got it. For Dedicated we can propose a straight reserve upgrade or staged canary rollouts. Question for you — is latency SLO more critical than cost at peak?
00:55 Lydia: Latency is important for checkout flows, we need p95 < 250ms for text gen endpoints. Cost matters but we're willing to pay for predictable tail latency.
01:10 Priya: On infra side, we need VPC peering, KMS integration for key management, and audit log retention for 12 months. Also want to understand if Redwood Private is necessary or if Dedicated in a customer VPC suffices.
01:30 Samira: Right — so options: 1) Upgrade Dedicated pool (reserved 2x) in US with EU add-on region; 2) Move to Private (VPC + on-prem options) for strict residency; 3) Mixed routing — host EU with a regional Dedicated pool. Each has different pricing and lead time.
01:46 Tom: Procurement — we need term options: 12 vs 24 month, and early termination clauses. Also, any discounts for committed throughput?
01:58 Samira: Yes, we can provide tiered discounts for 12/24 month commits and for higher reserved capacity. I'll send concrete numbers.
02:12 Evan: From performance side, we'll need to run a benchmark using your typical traffic pattern and sequence lengths — that will tell us whether 2x capacity meets p95 under target. We'll also test KV cache behaviour and memory for long context.
02:30 Lydia: A note — our peak sequences average 1.2k tokens with some spikes to 3k for chat transcripts, so KV caching matters. We've seen some vendors drop KV cash during long runs — sorry, KV cash, meaning cache — which impacts latency.
02:50 Marcus: Also, compliance — SOC 2 plus contractual right to audit and encryption at rest with customer-managed keys is non-negotiable.
03:03 Rohit: We have SOC2 docs and KMS integration guides; I'll share those. For audit logs, we can push logs to your SIEM via S3 or syslog.
03:20 Priya: Can you show an example of how KMS renewable key rotation works in practice? We have internal policies around rotation.
03:30 Evan: Yes, we'll include a flow: Redwood Dedicated supports customer KMS, key rotation, and HSM-backed keys in Private. There are some caveats on multi-region key replication — we'll document expected latency and failover behaviours.
03:50 Lydia: Great. On timeline — we'd like the capacity in place before mid-March onboarding. That suggests a 4-6 week lead time for Dedicated+EU. Is that realistic?
04:05 Samira: Yes, if we start the procurement and contract now we can hit mid-March. EU region lead time depends on capacity availability — we'll confirm in the quote.
04:18 Tom: Any blockers on data residency? If we host EU region for EU customers, do you provide guarantees on routing and log residency?
04:28 Evan: We can provide regional routing and guarantee that data is processed in the EU pool. Logs can be retained in-region or exported to your in-region storage. Will include options.
04:40 Marcus: About benchmarks — can Redwood run a mixed workload run that includes embeddings + generation + reranking? Our vault uses embeddings heavy on discoverability.
04:55 Evan: Absolutely — we'll simulate a mixed workload. Could you provide a representative pod of requests and sequence length distribution?
05:06 Lydia: We'll send a 24-hour sample and a condensed load generator.
05:12 Rohit: Action item — Evan will schedule the benchmark next week and join with Priya to validate results.
05:23 Samira: On contract terms: a 12-month renewal vs 24-month with deeper discounts. Also, we can include an escape clause for major infra changes.
05:35 Tom: We'll evaluate both. Also need supplier questionnaire answered (security + SOC2) — Rohit, can you provide that as part of the pack?
05:45 Rohit: Yes, will include supplier questionnaire and our compliance matrix.
05:50 Lydia: One concern — we had intermittent tokenization mismatches in a previous test which caused slightly higher token counts and cost. Any advice?
06:02 Evan: We can run an eval against your tokenizer and recommend quantization profile and batching settings. Redwood Optimize can recommend batching/caching profiles to lower unit cost while keeping latency targets.
06:18 Priya: For switching regions — what happens to session KV cache on cross-region failover? We need consistent user sessions.
06:30 Evan: Good question. Currently KV cache is local to a pool; for cross-region failover we can warm cache with prefix caching and use sticky routing. We'll document tradeoffs — cross-region will add latency.
06:48 Marcus: Competitors we evaluated: Anthropic for chat, OpenAI for some endpoints, and AWS SageMaker for self-host. We like Redwood's unified runtime and the observability dashboards.
07:00 Samira: Thanks — next steps recap: I'll send pricing and contract options; Evan schedules benchmark and preps infra scripts; Rohit shares security pack.
07:12 Lydia: Please include EU pricing separate and show delivery SLA for EU pool. Also include example SLO language.
07:25 Samira: Will do. Any last questions?
07:30 Tom: Procurement will aim to have initial PO ready by end of January if pricing aligns.
07:36 Marcus: One quick ask — can you include an appendix showing historical latencies from similar customers on Dedicated 2x? That helps our SRE.
07:45 Evan: Yes, we'll anonymize and include reference telemetry and dashboards.
07:50 Lydia: Thanks everyone. That covers it.
07:55 Samira: Great — thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and the benchmark invite.
08:00 (end)
